In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effectors of DC3000 are not individually essential but that their collective presence and activity is essential for the ability of DC 3000 to defeat defenses, and grow and produce symptoms in the host plants.
DC3000 uses its effectors to defeat plant defense by targeting two high-level processes, namely perception of external pathogenic signals and deployment of antimicrobials.

P. syringae uses the type III system to deliver a set of redundant effectors that are essential for bacterial growth in plants and are organized in a hierarchical fashion, with some effectors being essential for the growth of all strains and others being essential for the ability of only some strains to grow in plants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effectors of DC3000 are organized into a functional hierarchy that reflects their roles in defeating plant defenses.
the DC3000 effector repertoire has a modular structure that enables it to target a variety of plant defense processes, and that some of the effectors in the repertoire functionally overlap.
the effectors of DC3000 are organized into two groups: those with a primary function in growth and those with a primary role in defeating plant defenses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DC3000 effectors have been selected to work together to defeat defenses and that the redundancy in this system is a consequence of the collective nature of plant defenses.
